evidence.note: When compile errors piled up, agent chose to 'rewrite the entire compiler with a cleaner, simpler approach' — a wholesale restart forced by failure, not a targeted architectural refactor driven by a later feature falsifying an early design choice.

'AST definitions don't match codegen. Need to fix them.' — the closest thing to a cross-component design correction, but handled as a local patch to make types line up, not a structural rework of the type/AST representation.

The same class of bug (heredoc/shell escaping mangling source files) recurs repeatedly; the agent keeps trying new local tricks (printf, base64, Python, tee chunks) without a durable structural solution — symptom-patching and thrash rather than principled adaptation.

Parser rewritten completely after multiple syntax errors — reworking a failing component, but reactive to compile failures rather than to a falsified design assumption, and it never re-verifies unblocking a feature class.

reasoning: The trajectory never reaches the type/struct/ABI features that would expose an architectural limitation, so genuine design revision under falsified assumptions is largely untested. What is observed is repeated wholesale rewrites and local consistency fixes forced by compile/tooling failures (steps 205, 283, 313), plus persistent symptom-level patching of the same recurring escaping problem (127-368) without structural resolution. This matches the level-3 anchor (patches symptoms locally, same class of bug recurs) but falls short of it because the reworks are undirected churn rather than reasoned component reworks with re-verification, placing the observed level at 2.
